key_insight: UNSM changed the near-surface hardness of Cr3C2–NiCr coatings in a strongly sample-dependent way, with DS coatings reaching 820–970 HV and HVOF coatings spanning a wider 546–1165 HV range.
engineering_relevance: For wear-resistant coating design, the results show that deposition route and UNSM settings must be tuned together because local mechanical response and surface integrity do not improve uniformly.
method: Detonation-sprayed and HVOF Cr3C2–NiCr coatings were post-treated by ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification.
Four treated samples per route were tested at 20/30 N static load and 20/30 µm vibration amplitude.
Hardness was measured by instrumented indentation at 300 mN for 10 s, and scratch tracks were examined by SEM.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports measured hardness ranges for both coating routes, plus qualitative SEM observations of heterogeneous contrast and crack-like features after scratching, with mean friction coefficients listed as supplementary data.
watch_item: The scratch microscopy is qualitative and the abstract does not isolate UNSM-induced damage or support a definitive ranking of scratch resistance.
paper_title: HARDNESS AND POST-SCRATCH SURFACE MORPHOLOGY OF Cr₃C₂–NiCr COATINGS AFTER ULTRASONIC NANOCRYSTAL SURFACE MODIFICATION
